text: An Azure storage account is the single namespace that holds blob, file, queue, and table storage underneath it. You don't create a blob service on its own in Azure — you create a storage account first, and every container, share, queue, and table you work with from here on lives inside that one account, sharing its name, its region, and its billing.

Create a storage account with az storage account create, naming the resource group, region, SKU, and account kind. The account name has to be globally unique across all of Azure, not just your own subscription, because it becomes part of a public DNS endpoint URL. That's why names are restricted to three to twenty-four lowercase letters and numbers, with no dashes or punctuation allowed.

Every storage account picks a performance tier, and the choice matters. Standard is HDD-class infrastructure under the hood — lower cost per gigabyte, and the right default for the bulk of unstructured data: backups, logs, archives, and general blob or file storage where you don't need sub-millisecond latency. Premium is SSD-class — low, consistent latency and much higher IOPS, worth the extra cost whenever latency actually matters: a VM's data disk, a latency-sensitive database mounted over SMB, or a high-transaction blob workload.

Pair that tier with an account kind. StorageV2, general-purpose v2, supports blob, file, queue, and table storage together on either Standard or Premium, and it's what you'll reach for in almost every real deployment — the specialized Premium-only kinds only come up for workloads that specifically demand them. Read back exactly what you provisioned with az storage account show, querying just the SKU and kind fields.

One account, four services, two performance tiers — that's the foundation everything else in this chapter builds on. Next up: inside a blob storage account specifically, choosing between the Hot, Cool, and Archive access tiers, and walking through a real nightly-backup scenario to decide which tier fits which part of that backup's life.
